opening.argument: The discussion is financial-industry commentary examining Merrill Lynch's claim to support the fiduciary rule and whether that position has substantive application beyond retirement accounts. The advertisement is described as presenting Merrill Lynch as first among its peers in supporting the rule, while the speaker tests that representation against the firm's future conduct and the scope of its fiduciary standard. The analysis specifically considers whether the standard will apply to non-retirement accounts and says that, if it does not, the advertising may lack meaningful substance. This is skeptical evaluation of a firm's public claim, including the principle to “Put your clients interest first, put them front and center,” rather than an appeal to invest, pay, provide credentials, transfer money, or submit private data. The direct-to-camera office setting is consistent with that commentary.
